mainTopic: Blowing שופר on שבת: tied to the court's presence or the court's hours; then רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות of לולב and יום הנף.
overview: This amud asks how the שופר may be blown on a ראש השנה that falls on שבת after the Temple's destruction. In the first version, רב הונא's words 'ועם בית דין' mean only in front of the בית דין. רבא challenges this from the משנה's 'ועוד זאת', and the גמרא answers that in יבנה they blew only in front of the court, while in ירושלים they blew even away from it. In a second version, רב הונא's words are said on the יובל and mean only during the court's hours. רבא and רב ששת each challenge this from a ברייתא. Both challenges are answered: blowing is always limited to the court's hours, and on the יובל people may also blow away from the court. רבי supports the time limit. רבי זירא's question about judges who began to rise ends in תיקו. The גמרא then explains the four conditions for towns near ירושלים. A new משנה follows: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות to take the לולב seven days everywhere and to forbid new grain all of יום הנף. The גמרא gives a source for זכר למקדש and the reason for the יום הנף rule, and רב נחמן בר יצחק begins another explanation that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does 'with the court' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב הונא's phrase 'ועם בית דין' and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And with the court.' What does 'and with the court' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a short, unclear phrase from רב הונא about blowing שופר on שבת and asks what it means. It is setting up an explanation that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said the שופר was blown on שבת 'with the בית דין', but 'with' is vague. It could be about place (in front of the court) or about time (while the court is sitting). The גמרא wants to pin down which one.

keyTerms.meaning: The court (here, the great court of the Sages)

phrases.english: "And with the court."
phrases.notes: A quote of רב הונא's phrase about blowing שופר on שבת.

phrases.english: What does "and with the court" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up רב הונא's statement from the previous section of the sugya.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'with the court' refers to the court's physical presence or to the time the court is in session.

steps.title: It means in the presence of the court
steps.stepSummary: 'With the court' means in front of the בית דין. Anywhere not in front of the court, they do not blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means in the presence of the court. This excludes a place that is not in the presence of the court, where they do not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב הונא meant the שופר was blown on שבת only in front of the בית דין itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is read as being about place, not time. Blowing was allowed only where the court actually sat. Any other spot in town, even at the same moment, was not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presence of the court

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, in יבנה the שופר on שבת was blown only in front of the בית דין itself.

phrases.english: In the presence of the court,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין — דְּלָא.
phrases.english: to exclude [a place] not in the presence of the court, where they do not [blow].

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין, לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'With the court' means physically in front of the court. Any place not in front of the court is excluded.

steps.title: רבא objects from the משנה's 'and this additional'
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a challenge by quoting the משנה: 'And this, too, ירושלים had more than יבנה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection: "And this, too, ירושלים had in addition over יבנה," etc.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins an objection against רב הונא by quoting a line from the משנה. This step only sets up the challenge; the actual argument unfolds over the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists an advantage ירושלים had over יבנה regarding blowing on שבת. רבא focuses on the extra word 'ועוד' (and also). He will use it to show that רב הונא's 'in front of the court' rule cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (from an authoritative source)
And this also / and this additional thing
יבנה, the seat of the סנהדרין after the Temple's destruction

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
"And this additional thing Jerusalem had,
more than Yavne," etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attack on the explanation given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that in יבנה they blew only in front of the בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The extra word 'ועוד' in the משנה will be shown to imply something that contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: What does 'and this additional' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra words 'ועוד זאת' are teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does "and this additional" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the extra phrase 'and also this' in the משנה is coming to teach. It is setting up a search for the hidden meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'also' (ועוד) suggests a second, additional difference beyond what the משנה states openly. The גמרא wants to find out what that second difference is.

phrases.english: What does "and this additional" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the משנה line quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What additional advantage of ירושלים the word 'ועוד' points to.

steps.title: It can't just mean what the משנה says openly
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה only meant the difference it spells out, it should have said 'זאת' alone, without 'ועוד'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means what is taught [explicitly], it should have said "this" [alone].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the simple reading that 'ועוד זאת' only refers to the difference the משנה goes on to state.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Had there been only one difference, the משנה would have written just 'זאת' (this). The extra 'ועוד' (also) shows there is a second, unstated difference.

phrases.english: If you say it means what is taught [explicitly],
it should have said "this" [alone].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules out the simplest answer to step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'ועוד זאת' only refers to the stated difference.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading makes the word 'ועוד' unnecessary.

steps.title: First suggestion: individuals blew in Jerusalem, not in Yavne
steps.stepSummary: The extra difference might be that in ירושלים individuals blew on שבת, but in יבנה individuals did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: in ירושלים individuals blow, but in יבנה individuals do not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests what the hidden second difference is: in ירושלים private people blew שופר on שבת, while in יבנה only the official blowing happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first suggestion makes the extra difference about who blew (individuals or not), not about place or time. If it were true, it would not contradict רב הונא, but the next step will knock it down.

keyTerms.meaning: Individuals (private people, not the official blower)

phrases.english: Rather: in Jerusalem individuals blow,
but in Yavne individuals do not blow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new meaning for 'ועוד' after the simple reading was rejected.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra difference is that individuals blew in ירושלים but not in יבנה.

steps.title: But individuals did blow in Yavne
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reported that in יבנה, after the שליח ציבור finished, the noise of individuals blowing was deafening.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in יבנה individuals do not blow? But when רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: When the שליח ציבור finished the blowing in יבנה, a person could not hear his own voice because of the sound of the individuals blowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion of step 6 with an eyewitness report that individuals did blow in יבנה, so loudly that no one could hear himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If individuals blew in יבנה too, then 'individuals blowing' cannot be the extra difference between ירושלים and יבנה. The suggestion of step 6 falls, and the גמרא must find another meaning for 'ועוד'.

keyTerms.meaning: When [he] came [from ארץ ישראל to בבל]
The שליח ציבור, the prayer leader
The sound in his own ears / his own voice

phrases.english: And in Yavne individuals do not blow?
But when [he] came,
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said:
When the prayer leader finished
the blowing in Yavne,
a person could not hear the sound in his own ears
because of the sound of the individuals' blowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְיַבְנֶה אֵין תּוֹקְעִין יְחִידִין? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refutes the suggestion of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that individuals did not blow in יבנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An eyewitness report says many individuals blew in יבנה after the prayer leader finished.

steps.title: Second suggestion: the difference is the court's hours
steps.stepSummary: In ירושלים they blew all day. In יבנה they blew only during the hours the בית דין was in session.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that in Jerusalem they blow both while the court is in session and while the court is not in session, and in Yavne, while the court is in session, yes; while the court is not in session, no?
steps.whatsHappening: With the 'individuals' reading gone, the גמרא offers the remaining explanation of 'ועוד': the difference between ירושלים and יבנה is about time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים the שופר could be blown on שבת all day long. In יבנה it could be blown only during the hours the בית דין was sitting, which is understood as until midday. This defines the rule by time, not by place.

keyTerms.meaning: While the court is in session (during its hours)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'בזמן בית דין' (during the court's hours) with 'בפני בית דין' (in the court's presence). The whole challenge depends on the gap between time and place.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that in Jerusalem they blow
both while the court is in session
and while the court is not in session,
and in Yavne, while the court is in session, yes,
while the court is not in session, no?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו: דְּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם תּוֹקְעִין בֵּין בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the suggestion refuted in step 7 with a new reading of 'ועוד'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's extra word
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra difference was about individuals blowing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra difference is about time: in יבנה they blew only during the court's hours.

steps.title: So they blew even away from the court, against רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: If the rule in יבנה depended only on the court's hours, then during those hours they blew even away from the court. This contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that at least while the court is in session they blow, and even not in the presence of the court!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his objection: the משנה, read correctly, shows that in יבנה they blew even when not in front of the בית דין. That directly contradicts רב הונא from step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the only limit in יבנה was time, anyone in town could blow during the court's hours, even far from the court. רב הונא said blowing was allowed only in the court's presence, so the משנה stands against him.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's objection: if the משנה's 'ועוד זאת' is about time (the court's hours), then in יבנה they blew even away from the court, which contradicts רב הונא. The next step answers this by reading the difference as place, not time.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question of the sugya: is the permission to blow שופר on שבת after the Temple tied to the place of the בית דין or to the time it is in session?

phrases.aramaic: הָא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין מִיהָא תּוֹקְעִין,
phrases.english: This implies that at least while the court is in session they blow,
and even not in the presence of the court!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין מִיהָא תּוֹקְעִין, וַאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from step 8 and aims it back at step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's explanation that 'with the court' means in the court's presence (step 2).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule in יבנה was set by the court's hours, then blowing away from the court during those hours was allowed. That contradicts the requirement of being in front of the court.

steps.title: The extra difference is being in front of the court
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge to רב הונא. The extra difference is not about time, it is about place: in ירושלים they blew both in front of the בית דין and away from it, while in יבנה they blew only in front of the בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The difference is this: in ירושלים they blew both in front of the בית דין and not in front of the בית דין. In יבנה, in front of the בית דין, yes; not in front of the בית דין, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9 by giving a new explanation of the extra difference hinted at by 'ועוד'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said that if יבנה's rule were only about the court's hours, people could blow anywhere during those hours, which goes against רב הונא. So the גמרא changes the explanation. In יבנה, blowing had to be in front of the בית דין itself. In ירושלים, being near the court was not needed. This fits רב הונא exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presence of the court
Not in the presence of the court

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer for the משנה's 'ועוד': ירושלים allowed blowing even away from the בית דין; יבנה allowed blowing only in front of the בית דין.

phrases.english: No: for whereas in Jerusalem they blow
both in the presence of the court
and not in the presence of the court,
but in Yavne, in the presence of the court — yes,
phrases.notes: In יבנה blowing was tied to the court's physical presence.

phrases.english: not in the presence of the court — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by changing the difference from time to place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the distinction (presence instead of court hours)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The difference between ירושלים and יבנה was the court's hours, so people in יבנה could blow anywhere during those hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: The difference is presence: in יבנה blowing was allowed only in front of the בית דין, which fits רב הונא.

steps.title: Second version: רב הונא's rule is attached to a ברייתא about the יובל
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רב הונא's rule in a different place, on a ברייתא about the יובל. The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that every individual must blow the שופר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this rule of רב הונא on what is written: 'On יום הכיפורים you shall pass the שופר through all your land.' This teaches that each and every individual is obligated to blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of where רב הונא's statement was said. Here it sets up the ברייתא that his rule will comment on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'בכל ארצכם' as a requirement for every person, not only the בית דין. This is the starting point that רב הונא will limit in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach (a different version)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion against step 10. It is a second version of where רב הונא's rule was said, and in this version his limit is about time, not presence.

phrases.english: There are those who teach this statement of Rav Huna
on this, which is written:
"On Yom Kippur you shall sound the shofar
throughout all your land" —
phrases.notes: ויקרא כה:ט, about the יובל.

phrases.english: this teaches that each and every individual
is obligated to blow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the משנה discussion and brings another version of where רב הונא's rule belongs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From 'בכל ארצכם', every individual is obligated to blow the שופר of the יובל.

steps.title: רב הונא adds: together with the court
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the ברייתא. Individuals blow, but 'with the בית דין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: And with the בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a short limit to the ברייתא. The גמרא will next ask what this short phrase means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said everyone must blow. רב הונא adds that this is not totally independent of the בית דין. The exact way it is tied to the court is not yet clear; steps 13–14 explain it.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
And with the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְעִם בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Individuals blow the יובל שופר only 'with the בית דין'.

steps.title: What does 'with the court' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא meant by 'with the בית דין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'and with the בית דין'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of רב הונא's unclear phrase. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With the court' could mean in front of the court or at the same time as the court. The question forces a choice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is "and with the court"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רב הונא's words in step 12 mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'with the court' means place (presence) or time (court hours).

steps.title: It means during the court's hours
steps.stepSummary: 'With the בית דין' means during the time the בית דין is in session. When the court is not in session, individuals do not blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: During the time of the בית דין. This excludes the time when the בית דין is not in session, when they do not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא meant time: individuals blow only during the court's hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version רב הונא's limit is about time, not presence. So a person may blow away from the court, as long as it is during the court's hours. Outside those hours, no blowing.

keyTerms.meaning: During the time the court is in session

steps.whyThisMatters: This time-based reading is exactly what רבא will attack in the next steps.

phrases.english: During the time of the court.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, דְּלָא.
phrases.english: To exclude when it is not the time of the court, when they do not blow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'With the court' means during court hours; outside court hours individuals do not blow.

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא: blowing on שבת in the outlying areas, 'every man and his house'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: blowing on ראש השנה and on the יובל pushes aside שבת even in the גבולין, 'איש וביתו'. He will use this against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: The blowing of ראש השנה and of the יובל overrides שבת in the גבולין, every man and his house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins an objection to רב הונא by quoting a ברייתא. This step sets up the challenge; the גמרא first has to explain the words 'איש וביתו'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that even outside the מקדש the שופר overrides שבת, and it uses the phrase 'איש וביתו'. If that phrase means each man blows in his own home, it seems to have no limit of court hours. The next steps work out what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: He raises an objection (from a source)
In the outlying areas (outside the מקדש)

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
The blowing of Rosh Hashanah and of the Jubilee
overrides Shabbat in the outlying areas,
every man and his house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a challenge against the time-based version of רב הונא in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that individuals blow only during court hours.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא seems to allow every man to blow on שבת in the outlying areas with no mention of the court's hours.

steps.title: What does 'every man and his house' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'איש וביתו' means in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'every man and his house'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to define the key phrase, because רבא's whole challenge depends on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ביתו' often means a man's wife. But it could also mean his home. The meaning decides whether this ברייתא challenges רב הונא.

phrases.english: What is "every man and his house"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'ביתו' means his wife or his home.

steps.title: It cannot mean 'a man and his wife', because women are exempt
steps.stepSummary: If 'ביתו' meant his wife, that would make women obligated. But שופר is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are exempt from those.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a man and his wife, is a woman obligated? Isn't it a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא? And from every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא women are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules out the first possible meaning, 'a man and his wife'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing שופר only applies at a set time, so it is a time-bound positive מצוה. Women are exempt from such מצוות. So the ברייתא cannot be saying the wife blows too, and the phrase must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה caused by (bound to) time

phrases.english: If you say: a man and his wife —
is a woman obligated?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הִיא,
phrases.english: But it is a positive time-bound מצוה,
and from every positive time-bound מצוה —
women are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the first possible answer to the question in step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Women are exempt from a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, so they cannot be included in an obligation to blow.

steps.title: So it means each man in his home, even outside court hours
steps.stepSummary: So 'איש וביתו' must mean every man in his own home. That sounds like even outside the court's hours, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean: every man in his house, and even when it is not the time of the בית דין? (This is a difficulty for רב הונא.)
steps.whatsHappening: With 'his wife' ruled out, רבא completes his challenge: the ברייתא allows each man to blow at home, apparently even outside the court's hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing at home, away from the court, seems to have no time limit. That would go against רב הונא's rule that individuals blow only during court hours.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not: every man in his house,
and even when it is not the time of the court!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With the 'wife' reading rejected in step 17, completes רבא's challenge begun in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that individuals blow only during court hours (step 14).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Every man in his house' seems to allow blowing at any time, even when the court is not in session.

steps.title: No: in his house, but still during court hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'every man in his house' really means only during the court's hours.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, it means during the time of the בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא: each man may blow at home, but still only during the court's hours.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא tells us where a person may blow: even at home, away from the court. It does not tell us when. So it can match רב הונא's time limit, and the challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / in truth (keeps the original position)

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רב הונא's rule is about time: individuals may blow anywhere, even at home, but only during the court's hours. The ברייתא of 'איש וביתו' fits this.

phrases.english: No, actually it means during the time of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge of step 18 and keeps רב הונא's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא's scope (it speaks of place, not time)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Every man in his house' means blowing at home at any time, even outside court hours.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blowing at home is allowed only during court hours, so the ברייתא agrees with רב הונא.

steps.title: רב ששת brings a ברייתא comparing the יובל and ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא: the יובל and ראש השנה are equal for שופר and ברכות. On the יובל, every court blows and every individual must blow. On ראש השנה, only the court that made the month blows, and not every individual must blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: The יובל is the same as ראש השנה for the שופר blowing and the ברכות. The only difference is that on the יובל they blow both in the בית דין that sanctified the month and in a בית דין that did not, and every single person must blow. On ראש השנה they blew only in the בית דין that sanctified the month, and not every single person must blow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת brings a new ברייתא to attack רב הונא. This step only quotes the source. The next steps will work out exactly how it challenges רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two differences between the יובל and ראש השנה. One is which court blows. The other is whether every individual must blow. The second phrase, 'not every individual must blow,' is unclear, and the attack will be built on how we read it.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
The Jubilee year; the שופר is blown on its יוֹם כִּפּוּר
The special added blessings in the שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה (מַלְכִיּוֹת, זִכְרוֹנוֹת, שׁוֹפָרוֹת)
Declared the new month based on witnesses
An individual person, as opposed to the court or the community

steps.confusionAlert: The shofar of the יובל is blown on יום כיפור of the Jubilee year, not on ראש השנה. The ברייתא is comparing those two days.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
The Jubilee is the same as Rosh HaShana
for the shofar blowing and for the blessings,
except that on the Jubilee they blow
phrases.notes: Introduces the differences between the two.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בּוֹ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: both in the court where they sanctified the month,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁלֹּא קִידְּשׁוּ בּוֹ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and in a court where they did not sanctify the month,
and each and every individual is obligated to blow.
On Rosh HaShana they would not blow

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בּוֹ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: except in the court where they sanctified the month,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כׇּל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד חַיָּיב לִתְקוֹעַ.
phrases.english: and not each and every individual is obligated to blow.
phrases.notes: This unclear phrase is the focus of the next steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's challenge was answered, רב ששת opens a second challenge against רב הונא from a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that blowing happened only during the court's hours
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The attack is still being set up. It will depend on reading 'not every individual must blow' as a difference of time.

steps.title: What does 'not every individual must blow' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means when it says that on ראש השנה not every individual must blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not every individual is obligated to blow' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the unclear phrase means. This sets up the readings that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether רב ששת's attack works depends on what this phrase means. So the גמרא looks at the possible readings one at a time.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אֵין כׇּל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד חַיָּיב לִתְקוֹעַ?
phrases.english: What is meant by 'not each and every individual is obligated to blow'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵין כׇּל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד חַיָּיב לִתְקוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last phrase of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'אין כל יחיד ויחיד חייב לתקוע' on ראש השנה

steps.title: It cannot mean that individuals don't blow on Rosh HaShana
steps.stepSummary: Maybe it means individuals don't blow at all on ראש השנה. The גמרא rejects this. רב יצחק בר יוסף reported that in יבנה, individuals blew so loudly after the חזן finished that no one could hear himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that on the יובל individuals blow, but on ראש השנה individuals do not blow, that cannot be right. When רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: When the שליח ציבור finished the blowing in יבנה, a person could not hear his own voice because of the noise of the individuals blowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the simplest reading: individuals don't blow on ראש השנה. Then it rejects that reading with a report of what actually happened in יבנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יצחק בר יוסף's report shows that individuals did blow on ראש השנה, and many of them. So the phrase cannot mean individuals don't blow at all, and the גמרא must look for another meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a reading the גמרא is about to reject)
The town where the סנהדרין sat after the destruction

phrases.english: If you say that on the Jubilee individuals blow
and on Rosh HaShana individuals do not blow —

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר:
phrases.english: but when Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came, he said:
phrases.notes: 'והא' introduces the source that contradicts the proposed reading.

phrases.english: When the prayer leader would finish
the blowings in Yavne —
a person could not hear the sound in his ear
because of the sound of the individuals' blowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and knocks it down.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the reading 'individuals don't blow on ראש השנה'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: An eyewitness report from יבנה shows individuals did blow on ראש השנה

steps.title: So the difference is about time, which contradicts רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: So the phrase must mean that on the יובל they blow both during and outside the court's hours. On ראש השנה they blow only during the court's hours. The ברייתא therefore teaches that the יובל is blown even outside the court's hours, and this goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean this: on the יובל they blow both during the court's time and not during the court's time, while on ראש השנה, during the court's time, yes; not during the court's time, no. In any case, it teaches that on the יובל they blow both during the court's time and not during the court's time!
steps.whatsHappening: With the first reading gone, the גמרא proposes that the difference is about time. On that reading, the ברייתא clearly allows blowing outside the court's hours, and that is a challenge to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this second version, רב הונא's limit was said directly about the יובל: individuals blow the יובל שופר only during the court's hours. This reading of the ברייתא says that on the יובל, blowing goes on even outside the court's hours. That directly contradicts רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that (proposing the remaining reading)
During the time the court is in session
In any case, it teaches (pointing to the key line that creates the challenge)

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that on the Jubilee they blow
both during the court's time
and not during the court's time,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין — אֵין,
phrases.english: while on Rosh HaShana, during the court's time — yes,
not during the court's time — no.
In any case it teaches: on the Jubilee

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין!
phrases.english: both during the court's time and not during the court's time!
phrases.notes: This line is the point of the challenge against רב הונא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the 'individuals don't blow' reading, the גמרא adopts the time-based reading. This turns רב ששת's ברייתא into a real challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule limiting blowing to the court's hours
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the יובל is blown even outside the court's hours, which contradicts רב הונא's time limit.

steps.title: The difference is about place, not time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: it is always during the court's hours. During those hours, on the יובל people blow both in front of the court and away from it. On ראש השנה they blow only during the court's hours and only in front of the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, it is only during the court's time, and this is what it teaches: On the יובל, during the court's time, they blow both in the presence of the court and not in the presence of the court. On ראש השנה they blow during the court's time and in the presence of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב ששת. It rereads the ברייתא so that it talks about where people blow, not when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא separates two ideas: the court's hours (זמן) and the court's presence (פני). Both the יובל and ראש השנה are limited to the court's hours, so רב הונא is safe. The only extra freedom on the יובל is that people may blow away from the court.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches (rereading the ברייתא)
In the presence of the court, in front of it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'בזמן בית דין' (while the court is in session) with 'בפני בית דין' (in front of the court). The whole answer depends on keeping them apart.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer saves רב הונא's rule. It also shows that blowing on שבת in the court's town was tied both to the court's sitting hours and to being near the court.

phrases.english: No, really it is only during the court's time,
and this is what it teaches:
On the Jubilee, during the court's time — they blow
both in the presence of the court,
and not in the presence of the court.
On Rosh HaShana, they blow

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, וּבִפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: during the court's time, and in the presence of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: changing the difference from time (זמן) to place (פני)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets people blow on the יובל even outside the court's hours
steps.terutzMaskana: Both the יובל and ראש השנה are blown only during the court's hours. On the יובל people may also blow away from the court.

steps.title: רבי's statement supports this: blow only while the court sits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings support. רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רבי that they blow only while the court is sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רבי: They blow only as long as the court is sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer, and רב הונא's rule, with a statement passed down from רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says blowing happens only while the court is in session. That matches the time limit just defended. So רב הונא's position is not only defended, it has support from a major authority.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (introducing a supporting statement)

steps.whatToRemember: רב ששת's ברייתא does not refute רב הונא. Both the יובל and ראש השנה are blown only during the court's hours. The only difference is that on the יובל people may blow even away from the court. רבי himself supports the time limit.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said that Rebbi said:
They blow only
as long as the court is sitting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 24 and רב הונא's rule with a statement in the name of רבי.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that blowing happens only during the court's hours
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא בר גמדא in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רבי

steps.title: רבי זירא's question about judges who began to get up
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks about judges who stirred to stand up but did not actually stand. Does this still count as the court's sitting time for blowing שופר?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: If the judges started to get up but did not actually get up, what is the law? Do we need the בית דין to be sitting? If so, that is still true here. Or do we need it to be the בית דין's working time? If so, that time is over.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא asks a practical question about the rule from the last step, that we blow only while the בית דין is sitting. What if the judges already started to get up but are still in their seats?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to understand the rule. If what matters is that the judges are physically seated, they still are, so blowing is allowed. If what matters is that the court is still 'in session,' that session is effectively over once they prepare to leave, so blowing is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question that needs an answer, not an attack)
They stirred themselves to stand up

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
If they stirred to rise but did not rise, what is the law?
Do we require a seated court —
phrases.notes: Side 1: the judges' physical position is what counts.

phrases.english: and that is present here,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: זְמַן בֵּית דִּין בָּעֵינַן —
phrases.english: or perhaps we require the court's session time —
phrases.notes: Side 2: the session itself is what counts.

phrases.english: and that is not present?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the edges of the rule just supported in Step 25, that we blow only while the court sits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the rule defined by the judges physically sitting, or by the court's official session time?

steps.title: The question remains unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves רבי זירא's question unanswered: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no source that decides רבי זירא's question, so it leaves it open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means we do not know which side is right. Both understandings of 'while the court sits' remain possible, so the case of judges who began to get up stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question remains unresolved

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רבי זירא's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We do not know whether judges who stirred to rise still count as a court in session for blowing שופר.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about Jerusalem's advantage over Yavne
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that ירושלים had an extra advantage over יבנה. This is the setup for explaining its conditions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And ירושלים had this additional advantage over יבנה, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. This step only quotes it, to set up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that any town that could see ירושלים, hear the שופר there, was near it, and could reach it, could also blow שופר on שבת. The 'etc.' points to those four conditions, which the גמרא is about to explain one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: Yavne, where the סנהדרין moved after the destruction
Etc.; the rest of the quoted text

phrases.english: And Jerusalem had this further
advantage over Yavne, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד זֹאת הָיְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יְתֵירָה עַל יַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the court's session and opens a new section of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Towns around ירושלים that met certain conditions could also blow שופר on ראש השנה that fell on שבת.

steps.title: Seeing and hearing: excluding a valley town and a mountaintop town
steps.stepSummary: 'Seeing' excludes a town down in a valley. 'Hearing' excludes a town on top of a mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Sees' excludes a town sitting in a valley. 'Hears' excludes a town sitting on a mountaintop.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first two conditions by showing what each one leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition is needed because some towns meet one but not the other. A town in a deep valley can hear the שופר but cannot see ירושלים. A town on a high mountain can see ירושלים but is too far up to hear. A town must have both.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; this comes to leave out

phrases.english: 'Sees' — excluding one situated in a valley.
'Hears' — excluding one situated on a mountaintop.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the conditions of the משנה quoted in Step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A town must be able both to see ירושלים and to hear the שופר from it.

steps.title: Near and reachable: excluding a town beyond the limit or across a river
steps.stepSummary: 'Near' excludes a town beyond the תחום. 'Can come' excludes a town cut off by a river.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Near' excludes a town beyond the תחום. 'And can come' excludes a town that a river separates from ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the last two conditions, again by showing what each one leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a town that can see and hear does not qualify if it lies beyond the שבת walking limit (תחום שבת). Even a town that is close does not qualify if a river blocks people from actually coming. All four conditions must be met together.

keyTerms.meaning: Beyond the שבת walking limit (2,000 אמות)

steps.whatToRemember: A town near ירושלים could blow שופר only if it met all four conditions: it could see ירושלים, hear the שופר, was within the תחום, and had no river blocking the way.

phrases.english: 'Near' — excluding one situated beyond the Shabbat limit.

phrases.aramaic: וִיכוֹלָה לָבוֹא — פְּרָט לְמַפְסֵיק לַהּ נַהֲרָא.
phrases.english: 'And can come' — excluding one cut off by a river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of four conditions begun in Step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A town must be within the תחום and physically reachable, with no river in the way.

steps.title: New משנה: לולב originally seven days in the Temple, one day elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that at first the לולב was taken all seven days in the מקדש but only one day everywhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: At first, the לולב was taken in the מקדש for seven days, and in the rest of the country for one day.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It describes how the מצוה of לולב was kept while the בית המקדש stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מקדש, the לולב was taken all seven days of סוכות. Everywhere else, it was taken only on the first day. This sets up the next part of the משנה, the change made after the destruction.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of a new משנה
The palm branch taken on סוכות
The rest of the country, outside the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Here מדינה does not mean 'country' in the political sense. It means everywhere outside the מקדש, including the rest of ירושלים.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
At first the lulav was taken
in the Temple for seven days,
and in the country for one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה הַלּוּלָב נִיטָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה. It continues the theme of the previous משנה, which recorded another of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות, about שופר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the מקדש stood, the לולב was taken seven days in the מקדש and one day elsewhere.

steps.title: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי extends the לולב to seven days everywhere
steps.stepSummary: After the destruction, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a תקנה to take the לולב all seven days everywhere, as a remembrance of the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: After the בית המקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made a rule that the לולב should be taken in the country for seven days, as a remembrance of the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה records the rabbinic תקנה that changed the practice after the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra six days outside the מקדש come from a rabbinic תקנה, not from the תורה. The reason given is זכר למקדש: we copy what was done in the מקדש so that it will not be forgotten.

keyTerms.meaning: The leading sage at the time of the destruction

steps.whyThisMatters: This is why we take the לולב all seven days of סוכות today. It is also a central example of the principle of זכר למקדש, which the גמרא will go on to discuss.
steps.whatToRemember: Outside the מקדש, the תורה requires the לולב only on the first day. The other six days come from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנה, as זכר למקדש.

phrases.english: Once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the lulav be taken in the country for seven days,
in remembrance of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the change made to the original practice described in Step 31.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the destruction, the לולב is taken all seven days everywhere, by rabbinic תקנה, as זכר למקדש.

steps.title: The new grain stays forbidden the whole day of the עומר waving
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its list of תקנות: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled that new grain (חדש) is forbidden for the entire יום הנף, the 16th of ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And [he also made a rule] that the whole day of the waving [of the עומר] should be forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds one more תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. New grain may not be eaten at all on the 16th of ניסן, the day the עומר used to be waved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law, when there is no בית המקדש, new grain becomes permitted at dawn of the 16th of ניסן. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי extended the איסור through the whole day, so it is permitted only from the 17th. The reason is not given yet. The גמרא will explain it below.

keyTerms.meaning: The day of waving: the 16th of ניסן, when the עומר was waved and offered
New grain of this year's crop, forbidden until the עומר permits it

phrases.english: And that the day of waving
phrases.notes: Still listing what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי instituted

phrases.english: be entirely forbidden.
phrases.notes: Forbidden for eating new grain

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's post-חורבן תקנות after the לולב תקנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating חדש is forbidden for the entire 16th of ניסן, by rabbinic תקנה

steps.title: Where do we learn to make a remembrance of the בית המקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source that we do things as a זכר למקדש, which was the basis of the לולב תקנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And from where do we know that we do things as a remembrance of the בית המקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for a source for the whole idea of זכר למקדש. This sets up the next step, where it brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said רבן יוחנן בן זכאי had the לולב taken seven days everywhere as a זכר למקדש. The גמרא wants to know what basis there is for creating practices just to remember the מקדש. It is not attacking the תקנה. It is looking for its root.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
A remembrance of the בית המקדש
That we do / that we practice

phrases.english: GEMARA:
phrases.notes: The גמרא section begins

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we do [things]
phrases.notes: Standard request for a source

phrases.english: as a remembrance of the Temple?
phrases.notes: Refers to the reason given for the לולב תקנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה to the גמרא and asks for the source behind the concept used in step 32
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural basis for creating practices that remember the מקדש

steps.title: The פסוק: "ציון, no one seeks her out"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק in ירמיה that criticizes the nations for saying no one cares about ציון. This implies that ציון needs to be cared about and remembered.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the פסוק says: "For I will bring healing to you and heal you of your wounds, says ה׳, because they called you an outcast: 'She is ציון, no one seeks her out.'" This implies that she needs seeking out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a פסוק. Since the פסוק complains that 'no one seeks out ציון,' we learn that we are supposed to seek her out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is an inference (מכלל). The פסוק treats 'no one cares for ציון' as a shameful insult. That means caring for ציון is expected. After the חורבן, one way to 'seek out' ציון is to keep practices that remember the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: One who seeks out / cares for

steps.whatToRemember: The idea of זכר למקדש comes from the פסוק 'ציון היא דורש אין לה'. Since ציון should not be ignored, we must actively 'seek her out'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This פסוק is the classic source for all practices done זכר למקדש, which appear across many areas of halacha.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
phrases.notes: ירמיה ל:יז

phrases.english: "For I will bring healing to you
phrases.notes: Promise of future rebuilding

phrases.english: and from your wounds I will heal you, says the Lord,
because they called you an outcast:
phrases.notes: The nations mocked ציון

phrases.english: 'She is Zion, no one seeks her out.'"
phrases.notes: The key words of the proof

phrases.english: By implication, she needs seeking out.
phrases.notes: The inference: we must care for ציון

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 34
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From ירמיה ל:יז, the complaint that no one seeks out ציון implies that ציון must be sought out, so we make remembrances of the מקדש

steps.title: Why forbid new grain the whole day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about יום הנף again and asks for its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] And that the whole day of waving should be forbidden. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last תקנה in the משנה and asks why it was made. This sets up the explanation in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the מקדש, the תורה permits new grain at dawn of the 16th. So why did רבן יוחנן בן זכאי add a stricter rule for the whole day? The גמרא wants the logic behind this extra איסור.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new משנה. The גמרא is re-quoting the line from step 33 so it can ask about it.

phrases.english: And that the entire day of waving be forbidden.
phrases.notes: Re-quote of the משנה (step 33)

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁיְּהֵא יוֹם הֶנֶף כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the זכר למקדש source and returns to the יום הנף line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for extending the איסור חדש through the entire 16th of ניסן

steps.title: People might eat at dawn out of habit once the מקדש is rebuilt
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the מקדש may be rebuilt soon. People would then remember eating new grain at dawn the year before and want to do the same again.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Because] soon the בית המקדש will be rebuilt, and people will say: 'Last year, didn't we eat as soon as the east became light? Now too let's eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason. The worry is that once the מקדש is rebuilt, people will keep their old habit of eating new grain at dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תקנה protects against a future mistake. If people get used to eating new grain at dawn, they might keep doing it even after the מקדש returns. That would be too early. Forbidding the whole day breaks the habit in advance.

phrases.english: Soon the Temple will be rebuilt,
phrases.notes: The rule is made with the rebuilding in mind

phrases.english: and people will say: Last year,
didn't we eat when the east became light?
phrases.notes: When there was no מקדש, dawn permitted the grain

phrases.english: Now too let us eat.
phrases.notes: The feared mistake

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 36
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: To prevent people from eating new grain at dawn out of habit after the מקדש is rebuilt

steps.title: Without the עומר, dawn permits. With the עומר, the עומר permits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains people's mistake. Last year dawn permitted the grain because there was no עומר. Once the עומר is brought again, only the עומר permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they will not know that last year, when there was no עומר, the dawn permitted. Now that there is an עומר, the עומר permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation by showing why eating at dawn would be wrong once the מקדש is rebuilt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What permits the new grain depends on whether the מקדש stands. Without it, the arrival of the day (dawn) permits. With it, the actual offering of the עומר permits. Since the עומר is brought later in the day, eating at dawn would be eating forbidden חדש. The full-day ban keeps people from confusing the two systems.

keyTerms.meaning: The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן that permits new grain

steps.whatToRemember: With a מקדש, the עומר offering permits new grain. Without one, dawn of the 16th permits it. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole day so people would not keep the 'dawn' habit after the מקדש is rebuilt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the halacha keeps חדש forbidden throughout the 16th of ניסן even today, as a fence for the time the מקדש is rebuilt.

phrases.english: But they do not know
that last year there was no omer,
phrases.notes: No מקדש, so no offering

phrases.english: [so] the east becoming light permitted.
phrases.notes: Dawn itself permitted the grain

phrases.english: Now that there is an omer,
phrases.notes: After the rebuilding

phrases.english: the omer permits.
phrases.notes: So one must wait until it is offered

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדְעִי דְּאֶשְׁתָּקַד לָא הֲוָה עוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reasoning of step 37 by spelling out the mistake people would make
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dawn permits only when there is no עומר. Once the עומר exists, the offering itself permits. A full-day איסור prevents confusing the two
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The full-day איסור on יום הנף guards against eating חדש too early once the מקדש is rebuilt

steps.title: When was the Temple rebuilt? If on the sixteenth, there is no problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the מקדש would have been rebuilt in this scenario. If it was rebuilt on the 16th itself, then at dawn there was still no מקדש, so dawn really did permit the new grain and the worry disappears.
steps.simpleTranslation: In this case, when was the Temple built? If you say it was built on the sixteenth, then the morning light of the east did permit the grain, because there was no Temple yet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pokes at the reason from Step 37 by asking exactly when the מקדש would be rebuilt. It tries the first option, the 16th of ניסן, and shows that the worry does not fit there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry was that people would eat new grain at dawn even though the עומר should now be what permits it. But if the מקדש is only rebuilt during the 16th, then at dawn there was no מקדש and no עומר. So dawn correctly permitted the grain, and nobody did anything wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Being built (here: the בית המקדש being rebuilt)
If you say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא will reject)
The eastern sky lit up, meaning dawn

phrases.english: When is it that the Temple was built?
phrases.notes: The גמרא asks for the timing so it can test the earlier worry.

phrases.english: If we say that it was built on the sixteenth,
phrases.notes: First option: rebuilt on the 16th of ניסן itself.

phrases.english: then the eastern light did permit it.
phrases.notes: At dawn there was no מקדש yet, so dawn correctly permitted the new grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the scenario behind the reason given in Steps 37–38.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that a rebuilt מקדש would cause people to eat new grain wrongly at dawn
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rebuilding happens on the 16th, dawn came before there was a מקדש, so eating at dawn was correct. There is no mistake to prevent.

steps.title: If rebuilt on the fifteenth, the grain should be permitted from midday
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא then tries the other option: the מקדש was rebuilt on the 15th. In that case dawn does not permit, but the grain should still be allowed from midday, because a משנה says the בית דין is never slow to bring the עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you must say it was built on the fifteenth. Then it should be permitted from midday onward, because we learned in a משנה: people who live far away are permitted to eat new grain from midday onward, because the court is not lazy about bringing the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second option, rebuilding on the 15th. It challenges the תקנה again, asking why the grain is forbidden all day if it should be allowed from midday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מקדש stands on the 15th, the עומר will be brought on the 16th. A משנה in מנחות teaches that people far away may assume the עומר was brought by midday. So רבן יוחנן בן זכאי should have forbidden the grain only until midday, not for the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who live far from ירושלים

steps.confusionAlert: The quoted משנה is not about the time when the עומר must be brought. It is about what far-away people may assume: since the בית דין is never slow, the עומר has certainly been brought by midday.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that it was built on the fifteenth.
phrases.notes: Second option: the מקדש already stands before the 16th.

phrases.english: Then from midday onward let it be permitted,
phrases.notes: The challenge: why forbid the grain for the whole day?

phrases.english: for we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: Introduces a source from מסכת מנחות.

phrases.english: Those who are far away are permitted
phrases.notes: People far from ירושלים do not know exactly when the עומר was brought.

phrases.english: from midday onward,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מִתְעַצְּלִים בּוֹ!
phrases.english: because the court is not lazy about it!
phrases.notes: The בית דין certainly brings the עומר by midday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאִיבְּנִי בַּחֲמֵיסַר. מֵחֲצוֹת הַיּוֹם וּלְהַלָּן לִשְׁתְּרֵי, דְּהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the 16th, the גמרא tries the 15th and finds a different problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: Why the תקנה forbids new grain for the entire day of יום הנף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה teaches that the עומר is always brought by midday. So, at most, the grain should be forbidden only until midday.

steps.title: The ruling is needed when the Temple is rebuilt late on the fifteenth or at night
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the תקנה is needed for a case where the מקדש is rebuilt on the 15th close to sunset, or at night. Then there may not be time to prepare the עומר by midday, so the grain must be forbidden all day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where the Temple was built on the fifteenth close to sunset. Or, alternatively, where it was built at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 40 by picking a narrow timing case. In that case the whole-day ban really makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the עומר is ready by midday assumes the בית דין had normal time to prepare. If the מקדש is rebuilt just before sunset on the 15th, or during the night, the preparations might not be finished by midday. So eating at midday could turn out to be eating before the עומר was brought, and the whole day must be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: The whole-day ban of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, according to this approach, covers the case where the מקדש is rebuilt so late that the עומר might not be brought by midday.

phrases.english: It is needed only where it was built on the fifteenth
phrases.notes: Narrows the case.

phrases.english: close to sunset.
phrases.notes: Too late to prepare the עומר properly.

phrases.english: Alternatively, where it was built at night.
phrases.notes: On the night of the 16th, with no time to cut and prepare the עומר.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נִצְרְכָא, דְּאִיבְּנִי בַּחֲמֵיסַר סָמוּךְ לִשְׁקִיעַת הַחַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 40.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific timing scenario
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban seemed too broad, since the עומר is always brought by midday.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the מקדש is rebuilt near sunset on the 15th or at night, the עומר may be delayed past midday. So the full-day ban is justified.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a different explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts a new explanation of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new approach. רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to explain the ruling of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי differently, and the rest of his words come in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the reason was a תקנה made because the מקדש may soon be rebuilt. רב נחמן בר יצחק signals that he understands the ruling in another way. His actual reasoning comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who offers a different explanation
The תנא whose ruling about יום הנף is being explained

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
phrases.notes: The attribution, merged into this step.

phrases.english: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first explanation is defended, a new אמורא opens a different explanation of the same ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The statement is not finished here. רב נחמן בר יצחק is beginning a different reason for רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's ruling.
